title: Rays, Anchors, Phrases, Yields & Channels
description: A path that is a straight line out, a feed that holds your place, phrase-aware Japanese breaks, a task that steps aside, one state in three windows.

drops.title: Motion on a Ray
drops.description: A radial menu, a spoke loader and a spark burst, all travelling on offset-path: ray() with one angle each.
drops.concept: ray() is the forgotten corner of CSS Motion Path: instead of an SVG path it takes an angle and a size keyword, giving every element a straight line outward from its own offset-position. offset-distance slides along it, contain keeps it inside the box, and a radial layout stops needing sine and cosine. Three live clusters here share one set of custom properties.
drops.source: W3C — CSS Motion Path Level 1, the ray() function

interaction.mouse: Tap the hub to burst the radial menu; tap the spark stage to fire sparks.
interaction.click: The panel swaps ray size keywords, contain and offset-rotate live.
interaction.touch: Everything is pointer-driven; the panel hides below 760px.

drops.title: The Feed That Doesn't Jump
drops.description: Two identical feeds take new messages above the fold — one keeps scroll anchoring, the other opts out, with a drift meter in pixels.
drops.concept: Browsers quietly pick an anchor node in view and correct scrollTop whenever content above it changes size, which is why modern feeds no longer throw you out of the paragraph you were reading. overflow-anchor: none opts out, and this drop measures exactly what that costs: a watched message is tracked against the scroll container, so the drift readout is real pixels, not scrollTop.

interaction.mouse: Scroll either feed to the middle and watch the drift readouts as items arrive.
interaction.click: Pause, reset, or disable anchoring on the third feed.
interaction.touch: Feeds scroll with overscroll-behavior: contain; panel hides below 820px.

drops.title: Breaks That Know the Phrase
drops.description: The same Japanese paragraph wrapped three ways, every line box outlined, so you can see auto-phrase move the breaks.
drops.concept: Japanese has no spaces, so line breaking has always been free to split anywhere. word-break: auto-phrase runs a small on-device model (a C++ port of BudouX) to find phrase boundaries first and break there instead. It only applies to content marked lang="ja", which this drop lets you toggle — the breaks snap back to character-anywhere the moment the language attribute changes.
drops.source: Chrome for Developers — CSS i18n features (word-break: auto-phrase)

interaction.mouse: Drag the measure and font-size sliders to find widths where the two columns disagree.
interaction.click: Toggle line boxes, swap the sample text, flip lang="ja" to lang="en".
interaction.touch: Columns stack on narrow screens; the comparison badge still reports whether breaks differ.

drops.title: The Button That Yields
drops.description: One workload, three schedulers — tap the latency meter while each runs and watch the longest frame collapse.
drops.concept: Long tasks make a page feel broken: the spinner freezes and taps queue up behind the work. await scheduler.yield() breaks a job into chunks whose continuations resume ahead of other pending tasks, unlike setTimeout(0), which sends the rest of your work to the back of the queue. The three cards run identical work and report total time, longest frame and taps handled.
drops.source: Core Web Vitals — yielding to the main thread

interaction.mouse: Press Run on a card, then keep tapping the latency button while it works.
interaction.click: The panel changes workload size, per-unit cost and the scheduler priority.
interaction.touch: Cards stack; the tap target and readouts stay full width.

drops.title: One Component, Every Window
drops.description: Three windows share one state over a BroadcastChannel, with leader election, presence count and late joiners.
drops.concept: BroadcastChannel is a same-origin bus that any tab, window, iframe or worker can join by name — no server, no storage events, structured clone included. Each pane here heartbeats its presence, the lowest id elects itself leader, and a late joiner shouts hello so the leader can answer with the current state. Mute a pane to watch the others drift apart.
drops.source: Steve Kinney — Broadcast Channel for cross-tab UI

interaction.mouse: Change the accent, counter or checkboxes in any pane and watch the others follow.
interaction.click: Open a real fourth window from the panel, rename the channel, or mute a pane.
interaction.touch: Panes stack vertically below 800px and stay in sync.
